In the FY2022 10-K (Item 7A), Martin Marietta says cement prices are highly sensitive to supply and demand. Increases in industry production capacity or in cement imports tend to create an oversupply and an imbalance between supply and demand, which can hurt product prices, and the company cannot assure that prices will not decline with a material adverse effect [1].

- **Cement business:** a hypothetical 10% change in the sales price of the cement product line would change cement product line revenues by $60.2 million [1].
- **Ready mixed concrete business:** cement is a key raw material, and the company may be unable to pass cost increases through to customers. A hypothetical 10% change in cement costs in 2023 versus 2022, at constant volumes, would change ready mixed concrete cost of sales by $26.2 million [1].
- **Offsetting effect:** higher cement prices may hurt ready mixed concrete profitability while the cement business benefits, though the positive impact may not directly correlate [1].
